qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md ('A negative needs a successful control')
evidence: Most negative legs are well paired: functional prompt.md:32 and :49-50 require every refusal to pair with a same-kind success in the same criterion, and each criterion names its control (e.g. signin_and_client_scope Part A/B positive controls, judge.toml:45-49; wall_every_route Sian's thread/search/transcript and Dev's JUDGE-W1 reply, :59-65; hold_scope_and_release H3 delete and Insurer release, :152-159; deleted_and_expired 'Clause 14 noted' found and one-second-younger message shown, :119-126; search_and_transcript Part C '1000 pounds', :260; refusal_in_place right-password sign-in; render gate pairs 'nothing private before sign-in' with Gwen's sign-in). The exception is the persistence criterion (functional/judge.toml:266-280, weight 2.0/42): its legs are all 'reads exactly as before' comparisons and line 278 explicitly waives the controls: 'This criterion grades only durability: a feature that did not work before the restart is graded in its own criterion, not here.' Step c (:274) records whether S0 shows edited, whether S1 is On hold, the M-12 timer, whether Sian is walled, etc., with no requirement that those writes actually took effect, so a dead edit/hold/timer/wall feature earns durability credit by doing nothing, contrary to REVIEW_POLICY 'A dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing.' Minor secondary gap: timer_changes leg 3 (:139) 'Change the timer to off: the probate message does not come back' has no check that the timer reads off, though the criterion still has strong positive legs (7-day/30-day readbacks), so it cannot be earned by a dead app. No run exercised this weak-app case: raw-evidence-index.json scope says reward discrimination runs on these bytes are absent.
counterexample: An app that stores posts and replies durably in SQLite (passes the constraints gate, judge.toml post+reload+second-context) but whose edit, hold, timer and wall controls are absent or no-ops. In persistence step c the judge notes 'JUDGE-S0 not edited, JUDGE-S1 not On hold, M-12 timer off, Sian still sees M-11'; after restart_app all of these read identically, so persistence scores 2.0/42 of functional. Meanwhile a conforming-but-imperfect app whose holds work but are lost on restart scores 0 here, so the no-holds app outranks it on this criterion. The 0.05 functional floor (scoring.toml:11) does not neutralise this once any other criterion passes.
suggested_fix: In persistence, make the pre-restart state a positive control: before calling restart_app, JUDGE-S1 must sit under JUDGE-S0, JUDGE-S0 must show edited, JUDGE-S1 must show On hold, M-12 must read 30 days, Sian must get not-available for M-11 and JUDGE-S2 must be gone, otherwise the criterion fails (replace the line 278 waiver); optionally have timer_changes leg 3 confirm the timer setting reads off.
